newsitem.title: UK: NWE high, low sulphur fuel oil soft.
newsitem.headline: NWE high, low sulphur fuel oil soft.

text.p: NWE low sulphur cracked fuel oil was softer on Wednesday alongside sagging futures and healthy supply, traders said.

An Italian utility bought a very prompt 25,000 tonne cargo, meeting ENEL requirements. The price was agreed half at $130 cif NWE and half on a floating basis, based on the published quotes of two reporting services.

A refiner sold a 50,000 tonne low sulphur cargo late on Tuesday to a trader. The price of the cargo, due to load in late November, was not known but it was thought to be around $1 or $2 over the high of published fob quotes.

High sulphur markets were softer too. Barges traded at $118 in the morning and prices moved little through the day. High sulphur cargo offers were pegged at $119 cif NWE, while the bids were assessed at around $117/$118.

A Turkish tender for 25-50,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel was re-issued. The specific gravity requirement was changed to 0.975, and bids into the tender were sought relative to high sulphur quotes, and not low sulphur quotes as previously required. -- Nicholas Shaxson, London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
